reply_text:
Don't merge this yet. The main job of the branch, removing duplicate contacts when imports overlap, doesn't work. I read the full diff and ran the code but didn't change anything.

**The bug (`src/dedupe.js`):**
```js
return [...new Set(contacts)];
```
This only removes entries that are the exact same object in memory. But the README says overlapping imports bring in separate objects that share an id, and duplicates should be matched by id. I merged `[{id:1,name:'Ada'}]` with `[{id:1,name:'Ada'}]` and got both contacts back, so `mergeImports` currently just joins the lists together.

A fix that matches the README (keeps the first contact seen for each id):
```js
function dedupe(contacts) {
  const seen = new Set();
  return contacts.filter((c) => !seen.has(c.id) && seen.add(c.id));
}
```

**Why the tests pass anyway:** `dedupe.test.js` only checks the case where the same object appears twice, which the broken code already handles. Worth adding:
- two different objects with the same id should come back as one, and it should be the first one;
- a `mergeImports` test with two overlapping lists (right now `merge.js` has no tests at all).

**Smaller points:**
- `byName` in `order.js` looks fine: it doesn't change the input, and contacts with no name sort first. Two people with the same name keep their original order, because JS sort keeps ties in place.
- If a contact has no `id` at all, my fix would treat every id-less contact as one and keep only the first. Decide whether that's what you want, or whether contacts without an id should be kept or rejected.
- The version bump to 2.2.0 and the CHANGELOG entry look right.

The only thing that has to change before merging is the dedupe fix plus a test that would have caught it.
